notes: SYSERR: checking for crash file only formats the context passed to perror after a non-ENOENT fopen failure. perror writes process stderr, not the player's descriptor; the caller is PC extraction (R1/R2/R5e).

SYSERR: OPENING OBJECT FILE only formats the context passed to perror after a non-ENOENT fopen failure. update_obj_file is called during boot before player descriptors exist; the literal is process stderr, not player-facing output (R1/R2/R5e).
The "forced rent", "idlesave", "UNKNOWN!", and "Deleting ... file." fragments only reach log() in Crash_clean_file; update_obj_file is its sole caller and runs during boot (R1/R2/R5e).

The visible "TimedOut" label requires RENT_FORCED or RENT_TIMEDOUT in the saved header. Under shipped free_rent=YES, normal quit and idle callers write RENT_RENTED with cost 0; Crash_idlesave, the only RENT_TIMEDOUT writer, runs only when free_rent is false, and RENT_FORCED has no assignment in src/. No current C runtime writer produces either label code (R1/R2/R4/R5e/R5g).

SYSERR: READING OBJECT FILE only formats the context passed to perror, which writes to process stderr; the same failure's separate NOTICE send to the player is already C-first proven by fault-crash-file@1 (R1/R2/R5e).
Both alias-delete error literals only feed perror on process stderr after file-open or unlink failure. The delete and rename call sites do not send these strings to a player descriptor (R1/R2/R5e).
